notes:
Chosen hook (option 0, 'US TARGETS CHIP RENTING ABROAD'). Clear in under 2 seconds: 8 (plain words, large cover text, reads in one glance). Curiosity: 7 ('renting' chips is an unexpected idea and makes the reader ask how that works). Concrete number or name: 4 (only 'US', no figure or company name; this is the weak point). Promise kept: 9 (slide 2 opens with the rule requiring licenses for chips and servers sent to data centers that may serve China-linked firms, and slides 3 to 6 back it up). Reader stake: 3 (no reader effect, and the post does not pretend to have one). Overall 7, a pass because it is strong on clarity and promise.

Other options. Option 1 '5 COUNTRIES NOW NEED LICENSES' has a number, but it is imprecise: exporters need licenses to ship to those countries, not the countries themselves. It is also a side detail of the rule (slide 4) and does not say what the story is. Option 2 '12M TPP IS THE NEW LINE' is jargon that a global reader cannot parse in 2 seconds. Option 3 'BUYING CHIPS WAS NOT THE ONLY WAY' is vague and in the past tense. Option 0 is the best fit for the story, so no better option.

hook_types labels. 'claim' for option 0 and 'number' for options 1 and 2 are honest. 'myth-flip' for option 3 is a stretch, because no myth is actually flipped; it only hints that renting is another route. Minor note.

hook_pick_reason. It has an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' statement (the articles state no effect on what ordinary readers pay, use or risk), and none of the options is about the reader. This is fine.

Optional improvement. A number in the first line would raise the score, for example naming 750 H100s or the five countries, but only if the headline stays plain and accurate.
